title: A programmable quantum photonic platform integrating coherent emitters
authors: Hanna Salamon, Mikkel T. Mikkelsen, Zhe Liu, Peter Lodahl, Severin Krüger, Arne Ludwig, Leonardo Midolo
abstract: Photonic quantum technologies require the integration of high-quality quantum light sources with programmable photonic circuitry to enable on-chip quantum information processing. Semiconductor quantum dots have emerged as a leading platform for quantum light generation, yet their monolithic integration with cryogenic-compatible, programmable photonic circuitry remains challenging. Here we demonstrate a programmable quantum photonic platform that enables simultaneous control of highly coherent quantum dot-based single photon emitters and reconfigurable optical elements at cryogenic temperatures. System-level integration enables individual electrical and optical addressing of active components on a single chip, allowing their concurrent operation while preserving coherent non-classical light emission. We demonstrate multiple quantum-photonic functionalities, including pure single-photon generation, two-photon interference, and resonant transmission and reflection measurements of integrated emitters. These results mark a step from isolated quantum-optical devices towards programmable quantum-photonic hardware platforms capable of combining coherent quantum emitters with large-scale photonic functionality.
summary: This paper presents a programmable quantum photonic platform integrating quantum dot emitters with a reconfigurable nanomechanical router on a single chip. The system successfully demonstrates key quantum functionalities, including single-photon generation and two-photon interference, while maintaining high coherence. This work advances the field from isolated quantum devices toward functional, large-scale quantum hardware.
main_problem: The primary challenge is integrating high-quality, coherent quantum light sources (like quantum dots) with programmable, cryogenic-compatible photonic circuitry for on-chip quantum information processing.
main_result: The authors demonstrated a programmable platform capable of generating pure single photons and achieving two-photon interference while actively routing light using a nanomechanical element.
method: The research involves characterizing quantum light sources using Hanbury Brown-Twiss measurements and demonstrating active control over photon paths and interactions using a NEMS-based photonic router.
model_or_system: The system is a programmable quantum photonic platform built on a GaAs chip, integrating individually tunable quantum dot emitters and a reconfigurable NEMS-based photon router, all operating at cryogenic temperatures.
key_observables: Single-photon purity ($g^{(2)}(0)$), two-photon interference visibility, resonance linewidth ($\Gamma_{RF}$), and transmission/reflection spectra.
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperatures ($\approx 5$ K), low propagation losses ($\le 7 	ext{ dB mm}^{-1}$), and high coherence confirmed by linewidth measurements.
main_assumptions: The primary limitations for scaling are identified as cryogenic packaging and electrical/optical interfacing, rather than the underlying photonic architecture.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the platform components, I-V curves, single-photon purity measurements ($g^{(2)}(0)$), and demonstrate quantum interference and resonant scattering using the NEMS router.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the platform, characterizes the quantum sources (single-photon purity, coherence), demonstrates active routing and interference, and finally explores nonlinear quantum optical responses like resonant scattering.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, hardware-level realization of integrated quantum light sources coupled to reconfigurable elements, which is a crucial engineering step toward scalable quantum photonic circuits.
